title: Effort that leaves you waiting

captions.physics: Repeating an action for its reward

meaning: Shared effort can leave you feeling motionless when continuing serves a promised reward instead of a free decision by you both.
text: Sometimes you do a great deal while the feeling of movement never arrives. The Devil in the physical position of Manipura describes repetition bound to a promised reward: making another attempt, holding onto an attractive chance and staying inside what you began. The Devil in energy identifies the motive, refusing to release what has captured desire. The Hanged Man in emotions leaves a sense of suspension from which another perspective may become visible. The Devil’s two roles bind action to its pull, while the emotional pause helps reveal the cost of that connection.

Suppose you are trying to complete a difficult level in a game you play together. Every attempt promises a nearby victory, but the whole evening now depends on “Again”. **A free decision can begin with permission to stop.** A brief pause helps you see whether playing together still interests you or whether leaving a result unfinished is simply difficult. Hearing both answers honestly restores choice to the activity.

The difficulty is treating dissatisfaction as evidence that you have not tried hard enough. You repeat the action to escape suspension, only to become attached to the next promised reward. A pause feels like defeat although it offers perspective. Shared will includes permission to reconsider a goal. An unfinished game can remain unfinished without devaluing your participation or the time you already spent together.
